Lesson overview:
- Level: A1 General English
- Unit: MODULE 1. FIRST CONTACT & PERSONAL IDENTITY
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: Numbers 0–20
- Materials: Vocabulary cards, audio for the listening, reading handout, COSYmanuals A1 grammar pages for singular and plural nouns with numbers 0-20.
Warm-up: say one word you already know for this topic.
Recycles can and classroom vocabulary from Lesson 1.5.
Recycled language from the previous lesson: zero, one.
Answer from memory: which word belongs to the previous lesson?
Which word belongs to the previous lesson?
Core Active Vocabulary (5 items):

zero — the number 0. Example: Zero comes before one.
one — the number 1. Example: I have one brother.
two — the number 2. Example: Two students are absent.
three — the number 3. Example: There are three chairs.
twenty — the number 20. Example: The class has twenty students.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• How many ... are there?
• There are ...
• I have ...
• One, two, three...
• Let me count.
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.
Which word means 'the number 0'?
Which word means 'the number 1'?
Complete the sentence with a word from the list.
Link the final -s to the next word.
two books and three pens
Listen and repeat three times.
Which word has the target sound?
Mark the stressed syllable.
Grammar focus: Singular and plural nouns with numbers 0-20.
Add -s to most nouns after numbers: one book, two books. Irregular: one child, two children. Ask How many books are there?
Controlled practice: choose the correct option.
Choose the correct plural.
Choose the irregular plural.
Complete the sentence.
Reading: read the text and answer the questions.
There are twenty students in the class. There are ten chairs and two tables. One student is absent.
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.
A: How many chairs are there? B: There are twelve chairs. A: And how many tables? B: Two tables.
Speaking: Counting classroom items and inventory check

• How many ... are there?
• There are ...
• I have ...
Writing: Write 5 groups of counted items with plurals
